headline: 3000MW loss: Two power plants shut down causing nationwide loadshedding
summary: Power Minister Iqbal Hasan Mahmud reveals technical glitches and weather conditions led to the sudden loss of 3,000MW of electricity.
details: Power Minister Iqbal Hasan Mahmud informed the National Parliament on Sunday that technical failures at two power plants have led to a massive loss of 3,000MW of electricity from the transmission lines.
The Minister stated that this sudden drop in power production has necessitated loadshedding across various parts of the country, including Dhaka.
According to the Minister, one power plant had to be shut down due to a 'leak' in its boiler tube, forcing a mandatory production halt.
Another plant's production stopped because rough seas in the Bay of Bengal prevented the unloading of necessary coal supplies.
Minister Mahmud described the situation as a national crisis and called for unity to overcome the challenge.
He expressed hope that the situation would improve within the next two days, which would subsequently reduce the frequency and intensity of loadshedding.
caption:
3,000MW of power gone. Two power plants shut down, leaving parts of the country in the dark.

Power Minister Iqbal Hasan Mahmud informed the National Parliament on Sunday that technical failures at two power plants have led to a massive loss of 3,000MW of electricity from the transmission lines.

The Minister stated that this sudden drop in power production has necessitated loadshedding across various parts of the country, including Dhaka.

According to the Minister, one power plant had to be shut down due to a 'leak' in its boiler tube, forcing a mandatory production halt.

Another plant's production stopped because rough seas in the Bay of Bengal prevented the unloading of necessary coal supplies.

Minister Mahmud described the situation as a national crisis and called for unity to overcome the challenge.

He expressed hope that the situation would improve within the next two days, which would subsequently reduce the frequency and intensity of loadshedding.

headline_marked: 21 [[senior police officers transferred]] in major reshuffle
headline: 21 senior police officers transferred in major reshuffle
summary: The reshuffle includes promotions and new appointments for officers ranging from Additional IG to SP rank.
details: The Ministry of Home Affairs has transferred and posted 21 senior officers of the Bangladesh Police, according to a notification issued by the Police-1 branch on Sunday.
The reshuffle includes officers of various ranks, including Additional Inspector General (Additional IG), Deputy Inspector General (DIG), Additional DIG, and Superintendent of Police (SP).
DIG Md. Mushfequr Rahman has been promoted to Additional IG and posted to the Police Headquarters.
Barrister Mohammad Mosharraf Hossain, former NSI Director (DIG), and DIG Md. Moniruzzaman have been appointed as Additional IG of CID and Police Telecom, respectively.
Faruk Ahmed, former Additional Director General of RAB, has been promoted to Additional IG of Highway Police.
Other DIG-level appointments include Proloy Chishim at PTC Noakhali, Mia Masud Karim at the FDMN office of APBN, and Mohammad Osman Gani at PTC Rangpur.
The order, signed by Deputy Secretary Touhid Ahmed on behalf of the President, is effective immediately in the public interest.
caption:
A major shake-up in the police force: 21 senior officers have been transferred.

The Ministry of Home Affairs has transferred and posted 21 senior officers of the Bangladesh Police, according to a notification issued by the Police-1 branch on Sunday.

The reshuffle includes officers of various ranks, including Additional Inspector General (Additional IG), Deputy Inspector General (DIG), Additional DIG, and Superintendent of Police (SP).

DIG Md. Mushfequr Rahman has been promoted to Additional IG and posted to the Police Headquarters.

Barrister Mohammad Mosharraf Hossain, former NSI Director (DIG), and DIG Md. Moniruzzaman have been appointed as Additional IG of CID and Police Telecom, respectively.

Faruk Ahmed, former Additional Director General of RAB, has been promoted to Additional IG of Highway Police.

Other DIG-level appointments include Proloy Chishim at PTC Noakhali, Mia Masud Karim at the FDMN office of APBN, and Mohammad Osman Gani at PTC Rangpur.

The order, signed by Deputy Secretary Touhid Ahmed on behalf of the President, is effective immediately in the public interest.

#Bangladesh #PoliceReshuffle #LawEnforcement #BangladeshPolice #News

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, bdnews24.com, The Daily Star, Somoy News, Prothom Alo
